title: Science exhibition and museum
source_note: Original ForLanguage content. User-provided recent-review notes were used only as topic-frequency signals. British Council materials were used only to verify public task format and word limits.

tasks.prompt: You have joined a local science and discovery club. Reply briefly to five member messages.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.
questions: Which science topic interests you most?
What day are you usually free?
Which type of exhibition do you enjoy?
Who would you invite to a club event?

tasks.prompt: The club is planning a public exhibition. Write a short message describing one exhibition idea that would interest local families.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.

tasks.prompt: Three members are discussing how to make the exhibition useful and attractive.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.
questions: What kind of display would help visitors learn something new?
Where should the exhibition be held, and why?
Should members receive a discount or another benefit? Explain.

tasks.prompt: The club announces that its next exhibition will focus on oceans and nature, but entry will now cost more than expected. Write an informal email to a friend explaining your reaction and what you think members should suggest.

tasks.prompt: Write a formal email to the club president about the new exhibition fee. Explain your concerns and suggest practical ways to keep the event accessible while still covering costs.
